# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams: where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.

When the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

Polskie studio rysowania żółwiem w 2D i 3D, inspirowane klasyczną Logomocją. Statyczna strona: bez kont, bez serwera, bez sieci w trakcie działania.

## Uruchomienie

```sh
bun install          # brak zależności zewnętrznych; tworzy tylko plik blokady
bun run build        # buduje statyczną stronę do dist/
```

## Struktura

- `src/lang/`: lekser, parser (pełna walidacja przed rysowaniem), wykonawca oparty na generatorze (krokowanie) i limity. `run(source, mode)` zwraca `{ segments, error }`.
- `src/controller.ts`: uruchom / krok / pauza / wznów / reset z animacją; harmonogram klatek jest wstrzykiwany.
- `src/workspace.ts`: szkice per tryb w `localStorage`, wczytywanie przykładów z ochroną szkicu (pytanie + kopia do przywrócenia), postęp wyzwań, linki (`#/p/<tryb>/<base64url>`), pliki `.logo` (pierwszy wiersz `; Logomocja, tryb 2d|3d`).

Po załadowaniu strony `window.logomocja` ma `version`, `run(source, mode)` (czysty interpreter, bez UI) i `open(source, mode)` (wczytuje program do edytora, rysuje bez animacji, dopasowuje widok i zwraca obietnicę `{ segments, error }`).

+bun run dev          # buduje i serwuje dist/ pod http://localhost:4173/
+bun run test         # testy interpretera, sterowania i funkcji aplikacji

+Ścieżka bazowa: `BASE_PATH=/Logomocja/builds/x/ bun run build`. Wszystkie adresy zasobów są względne, a routing korzysta z części `#` adresu, więc `dist/` działa z dowolnej podścieżki bez reguł przepisywania (odświeżenie na każdej stronie działa). `BASE_PATH=/x/ bun run dev` serwuje pod tą ścieżką.
+- `src/lang/`: lekser, parser (pełna walidacja przed rysowaniem), wykonawca oparty na generatorze (krokowanie) i limity. `run(source, mode)` zwraca `{ segments, error }`.
+- `src/controller.ts`: uruchom / krok / pauza / wznów / reset z animacją; harmonogram klatek jest wstrzykiwany.

+- `src/workspace.ts`: szkice per tryb w `localStorage`, wczytywanie przykładów z ochroną szkicu (pytanie + kopia do przywrócenia), postęp wyzwań, linki (`#/p/<tryb>/<base64url>`), pliki `.logo` (pierwszy wiersz `; Logomocja, tryb 2d|3d`).

+- `src/challenges.ts`: 7 wyzwań i sprawdzarka porównująca kształt rysunku (próbkowanie co 2 jednostki, tolerancja 2, bez względu na położenie, kierunek rysowania i odbicie lustrzane; rozmiar musi się zgadzać).
+- `src/ui/`: edytor (textarea z nakładką: numery wierszy, kolorowanie, znacznik błędu, bieżący wiersz), widok (Canvas 2D, w 3D własna projekcja perspektywiczna z kamerą orbitalną), dokumentacja.
+3D nie wymaga WebGL: rysuje go zwykły Canvas 2D, więc działa wszędzie tam, gdzie 2D. Jeśli przeglądarka nie udostępnia canvasu, aplikacja wyświetla komunikat, a edytor i testy dalej działają.

+Po załadowaniu strony `window.logomocja` ma `version`, `run(source, mode)` (czysty interpreter, bez UI) i `open(source, mode)` (wczytuje program do edytora, rysuje bez animacji, dopasowuje widok i zwraca obietnicę `{ segments, error }`).
+`Ctrl/⌘+Enter` uruchom lub wznów, `Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Enter` krok, `Ctrl/⌘+.` pauza/wznów, `Esc` reset. Na rysunku: strzałki, `+`, `−`, `0` (dopasuj).

+`bun run test` uruchamia testy na publicznych granicach: interpreter (`run`), kontroler wykonania, przykłady, wyzwania i przestrzeń robocza (szkice, linki, pliki). Testów w przeglądarce nie ma: w środowisku budowania nie było przeglądarki, więc interfejs sprawdzono tylko przez kompilację i przegląd kodu.

content.text:
Logomocja is built in `/work` and all 78 tests pass with `bun run test`, but I could only check the interface by building and reading the code. There's no browser in this container, so I never saw the app on screen, didn't click through it, and didn't call `window.logomocja.open()`.

**What's confirmed**
- **Build:** `bun install` and `bun run build` work with no dependencies. The output in `dist/` loaded correctly when served from `/Logomocja/builds/x/`: every file returned 200.
- **Interpreter:** the 13 standard programs run with no errors and draw the segment counts I worked out by hand (for example 768 for the snowflake, 255 for the 2D tree, 121 for the 3D tree). Their sources match the brief character for character.
- **Error handling:** tests cover error line and column, parse-time versus run-time behaviour, every limit, and procedure scoping.

**Test boundaries (what each covers and misses)**
- **Interpreter `run(source, mode)`:** the 2D/3D drawing, errors and limits. Misses the UI.
- **Execution controller:** run, step, pause, resume, reset, and editing during a run. It uses a fake frame timer so no browser is needed. Misses rendering and accessibility.
- **Product flows:** the 13 examples, challenge checking, and the workspace module (per-mode drafts with in-memory storage standing in for local storage, asking before an example overwrites a draft, a backup to restore it, progress, share links, `.logo` files). Misses DOM behaviour.

**How the TDD went**
- Most slices went from a failing test to a passing one.
- The expression tests passed on their first run because the first slice already handled expressions.
- The 2D pitch/roll test also passed early, at first only because those words weren't commands yet.
- Four expectations were wrong in my tests, and I corrected them against the brief. One example: the 2D tree draws 255 segments, not 511.
- Writing tests caught two real interpreter problems: deeply nested parentheses crashed instead of reporting an error, and the message for a sign spaced only on its left (`np 10 -5`) was unclear.
- Reading the UI code by hand caught two more serious bugs: any click on the page would have switched modes, and fitting the view while the studio was hidden produced a broken zoom.

**Decisions I made**
- **No libraries:** plain TypeScript bundled by Bun.
- **3D without WebGL:** the 3D view is my own perspective projection on a normal canvas, so it works wherever 2D does. That also means the "say why 3D is off" case never arises; there's only a message for a missing canvas.
- **Routing:** page addresses use the part after `#`, so any `BASE_PATH` works and refreshing any page works.
- **Challenges:** there are 7. A drawing passes if it has the right size and shape within 2 units; position, drawing direction and mirroring don't matter.
- **Shortcuts:** Ctrl/⌘+Enter runs, Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Enter steps, Ctrl/⌘+. pauses or resumes, Esc resets. They're listed in the studio and on the help page.
- **`.logo` files:** downloads start with a line `; Logomocja, tryb 2d|3d` so opening a file restores its mode.

**Open choices you might want changed**
- **Run-time errors in conditions:** a division by zero inside a condition is reported at the condition's first token, not at the operand.
- **Operation-limit errors at the end of a loop pass or condition body:** reported at its `]`.
- **Operation-limit errors at the end of a procedure call:** reported at the call's name.

Nothing is committed: git has no author identity configured here, and the brief says the final folder is what gets recorded.
